text:
Wyatt Johnston has the chances of a 40-goal scorer and the goal total of a checking forward. He has 3 goals on 8.5 expected, shooting 6.7%, and his last five games brought none on 3.0 expected. A big Skinner save for Winnipeg on Thursday was a fair summary.

The rest of his game is fine. He has 13 assists, nine of his 16 points have come on the power play, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 93rd percentile among forwards for chances from in front of the net last season. That is the profile of a player getting to the right ice.

Here is why we would not worry much: goals tend to follow chances, and our range for his shooting is nearer 16%. Last season Evolving-Hockey made a similar note, crediting him with 2.5 expected wins against 0.9 actual.

The cost so far shows up in our wins added, where his goals have swung a full win less than his chances. Our projection still has him finishing between 21 and 37 goals, 29 in the middle. What to watch is simple: whether the shot volume holds.
